examples.kotlin: fun findById(id: String): User? = users.firstOrNull { it.id == id }

patterns.rule: new ArrayList<>() / HashMap<>() become mutableListOf() / mutableMapOf().

examples.java: private final List<User> users = new ArrayList<>();

patterns.rule: A Java class made of private fields and getters becomes a Kotlin data class.

examples.kotlin:
data class User(
    val id: String,
    val name: String,
    val email: String,
)

data class Order(
    val id: String,
    val userId: String,
    val total: Double,
)

data class Address(
    val street: String,
    val city: String,
    val zip: String,
)

patterns.rule: for-each loops that build or test collections become map/filter/any/all/count operations.

fun findByUser(userId: String): List<Order> = orders.filter { it.userId == userId }

patterns.rule: Anonymous single-method classes passed as callbacks become lambdas.

examples.kotlin: fun findById(id: String): User? = users.firstOrNull { it.id == id }
fun findById(id: String): Order? = orders.firstOrNull { it.id == id }

patterns.rule: Single-method callback interfaces become fun interfaces so callers can pass lambdas.
A for-loop that returns the first match (or null) becomes firstOrNull { ... }.

examples.kotlin: fun findById(id: String): User? = users.firstOrNull { it.id == id }
fun findById(id: String): Order? = orders.firstOrNull { it.id == id }

patterns.rule: x != null ? x.foo() : default becomes x?.foo() ?: default.

examples.kotlin: displayName = user?.name ?: "Unknown"
summary = order?.let { "Total: ${it.total}" } ?: "No order"

patterns.rule: static members move into a companion object (or top-level declarations).
Anonymous classes that cannot be a lambda become object expressions (object : Type { ... }).
